purpose: Frozen held-out corpus; labels and rationales fixed before any evaluation run. Not for rule tuning.

cases.rationale: The cross-TU callee returns null on the mode > 0 branch and the caller passes the constant 1, then dereferences unconditionally.
The null check is delegated to a callee in another translation unit; its early return covers the dereference.
The header-inline wrapper substitutes a live static fallback for a null argument, so its return value cannot be null.
The callee exposes a file-static pointer initialized to null; the caller copies it into an alias and dereferences the alias.
Only a header declaration of the callee exists; no definition or stub is present, so its return contract is a missing fact.
The cross-TU container is initialized with a null first element and the caller dereferences front() unconditionally.
The only callee definition is masked behind an undefined build macro; whether any definition is linked is a compile-time fact absent from the sources.
Both guards cover only the mode > 0 paths; on mode <= 0 the null local falls through to the dereference.
On the kind == 0 path the function pointer selects the null-returning producer and the result is dereferenced unconditionally.
The conditional assignment can yield null, but the following guard repairs that branch with a live fallback before the dereference.
A default-constructed unique_ptr holds null; get() therefore yields null and it is dereferenced without a guard.
The dereference hides inside a macro whose operand is an extern callee with no provided definition; the return contract is a missing fact.
The callback pointer is defined in a translation unit that is not provided; neither its target nor the target's return contract is known.
